the detection and attribution of the observed warming of the ocean.

the ocean warming over the period 1955 to 2003 is significant, is not due to natural variability of climate and is likely to be caused by anthropogenic emissions of greenhouse gases.
the ocean is warming, that the warming is significant, that the warming can be attributed to anthropogenic influences on the climate, and that the warming is well represented in climate models.
the observed ocean warming is a result of anthropogenic forcing.

anthropogenic warming has already occurred in the ocean and that the models are able to simulate this warming.

the ocean warming is a robust feature of the coupled atmosphere–ocean system, and is not a consequence of model deficiencies or errors.
the observed warming of the oceans over the last few decades is well reproduced by climate models that incorporate the effects of anthropogenic forcing, but not by climate models that do not.
